items.statement: The methodology defines functional and design requirements, evaluates valve and actuator features, calculates required and available output, and determines operating margin.

evidence_quotes.quote_original: - Evaluating the available margin between the actuator output thrust/torque and the required stem thrust/torque (i.e. capability margin), and evaluating valve/actuator survivable thrust and torque.

items.statement: System-level review identifies worst-case safety-function operating conditions and component review determines minimum required thrust or torque and actuator capability.

evidence_quotes.quote_original: The system design basis review identifies the worst case operating conditions for which AOV must operate and maintain position to perform its safety significant function.

items.statement: The procedure provides a documented, standards-based engineering evaluation methodology for AOV design-basis review.

evidence_quotes.quote_original: This methodology is fully compliant with the suggestions and recommendations of EPRI listed in the document EPRI Air-Operated Valves Evaluation Guide [1].

items.statement: When evaluation shows a valve cannot perform its intended function, required maintenance is recommended to restore full capability.

evidence_quotes.quote_original: If engineering evaluation shows the impossibility of valves to fulfill their intended function, recommendation of required maintenance activities will be given with the aim of achieving full operating capability of valve and actuator.

items.statement: Evaluation results are issued as a numbered work report containing operating scenarios, valve parameters, capability calculations, and conclusions.

evidence_quotes.quote_original: Results of engineering evaluation of selected AOVs will be presented in hard copy form of Work Report with the corresponding document number.
